genetic_context.description: Germline biallelic SLC30A9 variant. Zygosity is left unset because reported patients include both homozygotes and a compound heterozygote.

evidence.reference_title: Case report: Birk-Landau-Perez syndrome linked to the SLC30A9 gene-identification of additional cases and expansion of the phenotypic spectrum.
evidence.snippet: However, in the patients described here, brain MRI showed cerebellar atrophy, which was not a cardinal feature of the syndrome from the primary report.

nodes.description: Zinc handling by SLC30A9 is disturbed. Which way the disturbance runs is the open question recorded in the two hypothesis groups: the founding study measured less cytosolic zinc in mutant cells, while later work on SLC30A9 as a mitochondrial exporter describes zinc accumulation.

evidence.reference_title: SLC30A9 mutation affecting intracellular zinc homeostasis causes a novel cerebro-renal syndrome.
evidence.snippet: This suggests that SLC30A9 has zinc transport properties affecting intracellular zinc homeostasis, and that the molecular mechanism of the disease is through defective function of this novel activity of SLC30A9 rather than by a defect in its previously described role in transcriptional activation of Wnt signalling.

nodes.description: Normal milestones to age one or two, then loss of speech and motor skills.

evidence.reference_title: SLC30A9 mutation affecting intracellular zinc homeostasis causes a novel cerebro-renal syndrome.
evidence.snippet: All affected individuals were born at term, following uneventful pregnancies and normal birth weights, reaching normal neurodevelopmental milestones by the age of 1–2 years, but then started to deteriorate, with first signs of abnormality evident in speech delay and motor regression.

nodes.description: Zinc is a structural, catalytic and regulatory cofactor across the proteome, so disordered intracellular zinc affects many processes at once. SLC30A9 is expressed everywhere, highest in cerebellum, skeletal muscle, thymus and kidney, which is consistent with a disease that falls on brain and kidney.

evidence.reference_title: SLC30A9 mutation affecting intracellular zinc homeostasis causes a novel cerebro-renal syndrome.
evidence.snippet: We showed that SLC30A9 (solute carrier family 30 member 9; also known as ZnT-9) is ubiquitously expressed with high levels in cerebellum, skeletal muscle, thymus and kidney.

nodes.description: A progressive hyperkinetic movement disorder, the most consistent feature across families.

evidence.snippet: Pathogenic variants in SLC30A9 cause a progressive autosomal recessive neurologic syndrome associated with a complex hyperkinetic movement disorder.

nodes.description: Renal sonography in the founding kindred showed hyper-echogenic kidneys that were normal in size and free of cysts, in the four patients with renal involvement and not in the two with neurological symptoms alone.

evidence.reference_title: SLC30A9 mutation affecting intracellular zinc homeostasis causes a novel cerebro-renal syndrome.

evidence.snippet: Despite phenotypic variability between the 4 families, all affected patients manifested with a progressive hyperkinetic movement disorder, associated with oculomotor apraxia and ptosis.

nodes.description: Children reach normal milestones for the first one to two years and then deteriorate, starting with speech delay and motor regression and progressing to severe intellectual disability, a hyperkinetic movement disorder, ataxia and oculomotor signs. Brain MRI was normal in the founding kindred; cerebellar atrophy appears in a later family.

evidence.snippet: Whole exome sequencing identified a single mutation in SLC30A9 within this locus, segregating as expected within the kindred and not found in a homozygous state in 300 Bedouin controls.

nodes.description: Reported in the later Middle Eastern family, where it was measured by auditory brainstem response, and listed among the syndrome's features by that paper's summary. The founding report does not mention hearing at all, so whether the original Bedouin kindred was affected is not established here. Its absence in the second reported proband was noted as an inconsistency.

evidence.reference_title: Case report: Birk-Landau-Perez syndrome linked to the SLC30A9 gene-identification of additional cases and expansion of the phenotypic spectrum.
evidence.snippet: the auditory brainstem response (ABR) showed severe sensorineural hearing loss

evidence.reference_title: Case report: Birk-Landau-Perez syndrome linked to the SLC30A9 gene-identification of additional cases and expansion of the phenotypic spectrum.
evidence.snippet: The syndrome is characterized by early-onset neurological deterioration, intellectual disability, hearing loss, oculomotor apraxia, and early-onset nephropathy with features of tubulointerstitial nephritis and hypertension.

nodes.description: An occasional finding reported in a later family, not a feature of the founding kindred. The founding report states that deep tendon reflexes were normal in all six patients with no abnormal pyramidal signs, and spasticity is a pyramidal sign. A later series reports mild lower-limb spasticity in one of its patients and states explicitly that two others had none, which is why no frequency is recorded.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical Phenotype in Individuals With Birk-Landau-Perez Syndrome Associated With Biallelic SLC30A9 Pathogenic Variants.
evidence.snippet: Mild spasticity and brisk deep tendon reflexes were present in the lower but not upper limbs, and Achilles tendons were tight.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical Phenotype in Individuals With Birk-Landau-Perez Syndrome Associated With Biallelic SLC30A9 Pathogenic Variants.
evidence.snippet: Neither of the boys displayed any spasticity, focal weakness, or any convincing signs of cerebellar involvement, although speech was moderately dysarthric in both.

evidence.reference_title: SLC30A9 mutation affecting intracellular zinc homeostasis causes a novel cerebro-renal syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Deep tendon reflexes were normal in all patients, without abnormal pyramidal signs, including clonus or Babinski.

nodes.description: Early-onset chronic tubulointerstitial nephritis on biopsy, without cysts or tubular dilatation, with hypertension and a tendency to hyperkalemia. It affected four of the six founding patients and none of the eight in the later series, so it is a variable feature of the syndrome rather than a required one.

evidence.snippet: Despite phenotypic variability between the 4 families, all affected patients manifested with a progressive hyperkinetic movement disorder, associated with oculomotor apraxia and ptosis. None had evidence of severe renal impairment.

nodes.description: Chronic tubulointerstitial nephritis on renal biopsy without cysts or tubular dilatation. Present in four of six founding patients and absent in the later eight-patient series.

evidence.reference_title: SLC30A9 mutation affecting intracellular zinc homeostasis causes a novel cerebro-renal syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Histological haematoxylin and eosin stain of renal biopsy derived from Patient V-15 at age 13 months revealed chronic tubulo-interstitial nephritis with no evident cysts or tubular dilatation.

nodes.description: In-frame three-base-pair deletion c.1049_1051delCAG, the founding Bedouin allele, later found again in an unrelated consanguineous Middle Eastern family and in four siblings of a third family.

evidence.reference_title: Case report: Birk-Landau-Perez syndrome linked to the SLC30A9 gene-identification of additional cases and expansion of the phenotypic spectrum.
evidence.snippet: Whole-exome sequencing detected a homozygous in-frame deletion c.1049_1051delCAG (p.Ala350del) in the SLC30A9 gene, which was the same variant detected in the patients from the primary literature report and the variant segregated with disease in the family.

nodes.description: Missense variant c.1253G>T found homozygous in two unrelated Pakistani families, one consanguineous and one not, which suggests a founder allele.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical Phenotype in Individuals With Birk-Landau-Perez Syndrome Associated With Biallelic SLC30A9 Pathogenic Variants.
evidence.snippet: In 2 unrelated families of Pakistani origin (1 consanguineous and 1 not), the same homozygous missense variant in SLC30A9 (c.1253G>T, p.Gly418Val) was identified.

nodes.description: Synonymous change c.1413A>G, carried in trans with a frameshift allele. cDNA analysis confirmed an effect on splicing, so a synonymous call here is not benign by default.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical Phenotype in Individuals With Birk-Landau-Perez Syndrome Associated With Biallelic SLC30A9 Pathogenic Variants.
evidence.snippet: For the synonymous variant p.Ser471=, an effect on splicing was confirmed through cDNA analysis.
